statement_blocker: The catalog does not choose a graph or weight model; a cut representation; an edge-count, capacity, conductance, expansion, or demand numerator/denominator; positivity and balance conditions; zero-denominator conventions; an objective/value/existence/inequality/algorithm theorem kind; approximation constants; or a computational model. Choosing uniform or nonuniform sparsest cut, conductance, balanced separator, a minimum-cut result, or the Arora-Rao-Vazirani approximation theorem would invent or substitute proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the vertex universe, graph kind, finiteness and decidability context, edge-capacity and demand functions, coefficient types, cut representation, objective codomain, and any algorithm/input/output structures.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not say whether the target defines sparsity, proves existence or attainment of an optimum, establishes an inequality or reduction, or gives an exact or approximate algorithm and complexity guarantee.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every graph, cut, weight, denominator, balance, optimizer, algorithm, and boundary case listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: definition and elementary properties of an edge boundary or cut capacity
existence of a nontrivial cut attaining minimum sparsity in a finite unweighted or weighted graph
uniform sparsest cut normalized by side cardinalities
nonuniform sparsest cut normalized by separated demand
conductance or edge expansion normalized by volume or smaller-side size
a balanced-separator existence or approximation theorem
an exact or approximate sparse-cut algorithm with an explicit complexity and probability model
a flow, metric, spectral, Cheeger, or expander comparison theorem
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, and other small vertex types
empty, full, ordered, unordered, nontrivial, and exactly balanced cuts
disconnected, edgeless, complete, and isolated-vertex graphs
zero, negative, infinite, or unsupported capacities and demands
zero denominator or zero separated demand and the codomain of any ratio
ties and nonuniqueness among minimizing cuts
strict versus non-strict balance and sparsity inequalities
exact, asymptotic, deterministic, randomized, integral, rational, real, and floating-point algorithmic conventions
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-0877 network flow, THM-M-0878 minimum-cost flow, THM-M-0879 multicommodity flow, THM-M-0814 maximum-flow/minimum-cut, THM-M-0831 Karger, THM-M-0832 Stoer-Wagner, THM-M-0881 expander graphs, THM-M-0887 spectral graph theory, or THM-M-0888 Cheeger inequality
the separate THM-C-0077 Arora-Rao-Vazirani O(sqrt(log n)) approximation record in Docs/researches/cs_theorems.md
minimum cut, maximum cut, conductance, edge expansion, balanced separator, or edge connectivity substituted without a source-selected relationship
a structure, predicate, or hypothesis that assumes the requested sparse cut, optimum, ratio, or approximation guarantee
generic edge-set, induced-subgraph, connectivity, coloring-partition, or degree APIs without an exact source-mapped theorem bridge
a fixed graph example, numerical optimizer run, benchmark, or empirical sparsity calculation
the catalog's untrusted verified label, a title match, or a bounded discovery query used as proof evidence
